We need to output JSON with rules extracted from policy. The policy is long. We need to extract each rule element with modality, target, condition, exception, temporal, participants, quote.

We must only output JSON, no markdown.

We need to parse the policy for rules: statements about what the agent must/should not do, etc.

We need to extract each rule element. Likely many rules. We need to be exhaustive? Probably extract key rules: e.g., "You should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments." That's a FORBID rule: target: provide information not from user/tools or give subjective recommendations. Condition: none. Exception: none. Temporal: none? Participants: maybe agent. Quote exact.

Also: "You should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time." That's a REQUIRE? Actually it's a restriction: you must not do both at same time. So FORBID: make tool call and respond simultaneously. Condition: none. etc.

"You should deny user requests that are against this policy." FORBID: comply with requests against policy. etc.

"You should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user." This is a REQUIRE: when request cannot be handled, you must transfer via tool call then message. Also PERMIT? Actually it's a procedure.

"You should try your best to resolve the issue for the user before transferring the user to a human agent." That's a REQUIRE: attempt resolution before transfer.

Domain basics: many descriptive, not rules.

Customer Lookup: "You can look up customer information using: - Phone number - Customer ID - Full name with date of birth. For name lookup, date of birth is required for verification purposes." That's a PERMIT? Actually it's capability, not a rule about agent behavior. Might be PERMIT: you may look up using those. Condition: for name lookup, DOB required.

Overdue Bill Payment: many steps: "Check the bill status to make sure it is overdue." That's a REQUIRE: before sending payment request, check bill overdue. "Check the bill amount due" REQUIRE. "Send the user a payment request for the overdue bill. - This will change the status of the bill to AWAITING PAYMENT." That's an action: you may send payment request? It's a step, maybe PERMIT? But it's required as part of process. We'll treat as REQUIRE: you must send payment request after checks. Condition: bill overdue. etc.

"Inform the user that a payment request has been sent. They should: - Check their payment requests using the check_payment_request tool." That's REQUIRE: inform user.

"If the user accepts the payment request, use the make_payment tool to make the payment." REQUIRE.

"After the payment is made, the bill status will be updated to PAID." That's outcome, not rule.

"Always check that the bill status is updated to PAID before informing the user that the bill has been paid." REQUIRE.

"Important: - A user can only have one bill in the AWAITING PAYMENT status at a time. - The send payement request tool will not check if the bill is overdue. You should always check that the bill is overdue before sending a payment request." So FORBID: send payment request if bill not overdue. Also maybe REQUIRE: check overdue before sending.

Line Suspension: "When a line is suspended, the user will not have service." descriptive.

"A line can be suspended for the following reasons: - The user has an overdue bill. - The line's contract end date is in the past." descriptive.

"You are allowed to lift the suspension after the user has paid all their overdue bills." PERMIT: you may lift suspension if all overdue paid.

"You are not allowed to lift the suspension if the line's contract end date is in the past, even if the user has paid all their overdue bills." FORBID: lift suspension if contract end date past.

"After you resume the line, the user will have to reboot their device to get service." outcome.

Data Refueling: "Each plan specify the maxium data usage per month. If the user's data usage for a line exceeds the plan's data limit, data connectivity will be lost. You can add more data to the line by "refueling" data at a price per GB specified by the plan. The maximum amount of data that can be refueled is 2GB. To refuel data you should: - Ask them how much data they want to refuel - Confirm the price - Apply the refueled data to the line associated with the phone number the user provided." So REQUIRE: ask amount, confirm price, apply.

Change Plan: steps similar: "Make sure you know what line the user wants to change the plan for." REQUIRE. "Gather available plans" REQUIRE. "Ask the user to select one." REQUIRE. "Calculate the price of the new plan." REQUIRE. "Confirm the price." REQUIRE. "Apply the plan to the line associated with the phone number the user provided." REQUIRE.

Data Roaming: "If a line is roaming enabled, the user can use their phone's data connection in areas outside their home network. We offer data roaming to users who are traveling outside their home network. If a user is traveling outside their home network, you should check if the line is roaming enabled. If it is not, you should enable it at no cost for the user." So REQUIRE: check roaming enabled; if not, enable at no cost.

Technical Support: "You must first identify the customer." REQUIRE.

Tech support policy includes many "guide the user to use ..." which are REQUIRE? Actually they are suggestions: "guide the user to use ..." maybe PERMIT? But policy says "You must understand those well since as part of technical support you will have to help the customer perform series of actions". So it's REQUIRE to help them perform actions. But we can extract some key rules: e.g., "If it shows 'Missing', guide the user to use `reseat_sim_card()` to ensure the SIM card is correctly inserted." That's a REQUIRE: guide user to reseat SIM if missing.

"If it shows 'Locked' (due to incorrect PIN or PUK entries), **escalate to technical support for assistance with SIM security**." That's REQUIRE: escalate to technical support.

"If `check_apn_settings()` shows 'Incorrect', guide the user to use `reset_apn_settings()` to reset the APN settings. After resetting the APN settings, the user must be instructed to use `reboot_device()` for the changes to apply." REQUIRE.

"If the line is suspended and the agent can lift the suspension (per general policy), verify if service is restored." REQUIRE? Actually "verify if service is restored" after lift.

"If the suspension cannot be lifted by the agent (e.g., due to contract end date as mentioned in general policy, or other reasons not resolvable by the agent), **escalate to technical support**." REQUIRE: escalate.

Many similar for mobile data: guide user to toggle_data, toggle_roaming, toggle_data_saver_mode, disconnect_vpn, etc.

MMS: guide user to set_network_mode_preference, reset_apn_settings, reboot_device, toggle_wifi_calling, grant_app_permission.

But instructions: "Extract a precise formal theory of the governing policy in the <policy> block. For EVERY rule element include an exact verbatim quote from the policy that proves it." So we must extract every rule element. That's massive.

Given time, maybe we can produce a compact representation focusing on high-level rules. But risk of missing.

Temporal: often none, but some have order like "first make a tool call, then send the message". That's temporal: anchor: "make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents", order: BEFORE? The action "send the message" must be AFTER the tool call. So we can represent for the rule about sending message after tool call.
